register.name: Government Pension Fund Global
register.detail: Norges Bank Investment Management · value on 30 September 2026 · return of -0.5% in the third quarter of 2026 · 80 billion kroner added after management costs in the quarter
register.note: The market value of the investment portfolio was 22,025 billion kroner at the same date
register.text: The nation’s oil and gas revenue, invested abroad in equities, bonds, real estate and renewable energy infrastructure. It returned -0.5% in the third quarter of 2026, or -278 billion kroner, while 80 billion kroner was added to it after management costs.

register.name: Twenty-year government bond (NGB 09/2046, 4.500%)
register.detail: Kingdom of Norway · priced by syndication 15 September 2026 · settled 24 September 2026 · due 24 September 2046 · coupon 4.500% · reoffer yield 4.509% · orders above NOK 59bn from more than 60 investors
register.note: NOK 10bn allocated to investors and NOK 4bn retained by the issuer for repo purposes
register.text: A new twenty-year Norwegian Government Bond, sold by syndication through Government Debt Management at Norges Bank. The government borrows to finance capital transactions, including government lending schemes such as the lending of the Norwegian State Housing Bank and the State Educational Loan Fund, and the redemption of existing debt; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Ten-year government bond (NGB 06/2036, 4.125%)
register.detail: Kingdom of Norway · new bond priced by syndication 27 January 2026, settled 3 February 2026 · reoffer yield 4.243% · tap issue of NOK 15bn priced 12 May 2026 at a reoffer yield of 4.532% · due 3 June 2036
register.note: NOK 20bn allocated to investors and NOK 4bn retained for repo purposes; orders above NOK 83bn for the new bond and above NOK 78bn for the tap
register.text: A new ten-year Norwegian Government Bond, sold by syndication in January 2026 and enlarged by a NOK 15 billion tap issue in May 2026. It finances the government’s capital transactions, among them the lending of the state housing and student loan institutions, and the redemption of existing debt; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of the seven standards.

register.name: Norwegian State Housing Bank (Husbanken), 2025
register.detail: Husbanken · annual report 2025, dated 13 March 2026 · loan framework NOK 34bn · start-up loans of over NOK 16bn to 7,428 households through the municipalities · grant commitments NOK 4.6bn · housing allowance of about NOK 4.1bn · loans committed to build nearly 3,000 homes
register.note: About 134,100 households with low incomes and high housing costs received the housing allowance; loan portfolio of about NOK 196bn at the end of 2025
register.text: The state housing bank, whose mission is to prevent people from becoming disadvantaged in the housing market. It lends to the municipalities for start-up loans (startlån) that help households buy a home, lends for new and better homes, commits grants and pays the housing allowance (bostøtte); it serves the shelter standard, the standard furthest from reach in Norway.

register.name: Kommunalbanken green loans to local government, 2025
register.detail: Kommunalbanken (KBN) · annual report 2025, 12 March 2026 · NOK 75.7bn in green loans across 570 local government projects at the end of 2025 · 21% of the lending portfolio · financed by KBN green bonds
register.note: KBN is 100% owned by the Norwegian state and is the largest lender to the local government sector; aggregate loans to customers of NOK 374,007 million
register.text: Green loans from KBN, the state-owned municipal lender, financed by green bonds that fund the transition to a low-carbon, climate-resilient future in Norwegian local communities. KBN lends to municipalities and counties particularly in education, health and care services and water and wastewater infrastructure, which serve the education, health and water standards and the shelter standard, measured in Norway by safely managed sanitation.

register.name: Government borrowing programme, 2026
register.detail: Norges Bank, Government Debt Management · strategy of 12 December 2025 · a new ten-year and a new twenty-year bond · net new lending budgeted for 2026: NOK 17.2bn by the Norwegian State Housing Bank and NOK 20.9bn by the Norwegian State Educational Loan Fund
register.note: Planned issuance of government bonds in 2026; net new lending by state lending institutions of NOK 40.5bn in 2026
register.text: The plan to issue between NOK 100 billion and NOK 110 billion in government bonds in 2026, to finance capital transactions including government lending schemes and the redemption of existing debt. The borrowing requirement includes net new lending by the Norwegian State Housing Bank and the Norwegian State Educational Loan Fund, which serve the shelter and education standards.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Oil and Gas
items.label: Of GDP from oil and gas rents, 2021
items.text: Oil and gas already earn; the task is to turn the rent into assets that outlast it.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 15.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: Holdbart
items.text: A Norwegian company that buys surplus food that retailers cannot sell through normal channels and resells it at lower prices so that “good food reaches people who need it”, with 23 stores across Norway in 2025 and 13,746 tons of food saved in 2024.

items.name: Forskerfabrikken
items.text: A social enterprise that works to increase children’s understanding of how science and technology shape individuals, society and nature, through hands-on learning and nationwide programmes for Norwegian children.

items.name: KLAR
items.text: A digital learning tool that introduces multilingual learners to the professional language used in education, so that more students complete vocational upper secondary education and move into work; its customers include county authorities, schools and adult education providers.

items.name: Motitech
items.text: A motivational tool that encourages physical activity among older adults and people with dementia, designed to prevent falls, improve health outcomes and enhance quality of life.

items.name: Lifetools
items.text: The maker of KnowMe, a digital communication tool that helps people with communication challenges express themselves, with measurable gains in participation, self-expression and social inclusion reported by the company.

items.name: GET Academy
items.text: A vocational education programme for young people outside the labour market: a 20-week intensive coding course followed by a year of work placement with a mentor.

items.name: Gammel Nok
items.text: A company headquartered in Asker, now also in Hamar and Østfold, whose workers are all aged 50 or over and which delivers staffing, practical services and home-based care to private and public clients, employing more than 400 senior workers.
